title: RT-DETRv4: Painlessly Furthering Real-Time Object Detection with Vision Foundation Models

problem.summary: Real-time detectors trade feature quality for speed, and RT-DETR's AIFI output is only indirectly supervised, creating a semantic bottleneck; transferring foundation-model semantics is hard because teachers and resource-constrained detectors differ in architecture and learning objective.
statements: High-speed inference via lightweight networks leads to degraded feature representation and hurts on-device deployment
Real-time constraints force lightweight backbones that cannot capture high-level semantics, causing a semantic bottleneck
The AIFI output F5 receives only indirect supervision from detection losses and may be insufficiently optimized
Architectural and learning-objective disparities between VFMs and detectors make stable, task-aligned semantic transfer difficult

evidence.quote: However, the pursuit of high-speed inference via lightweight network designs often leads to degraded feature representation, which hinders further performance improvements and practical on-device deployment.

To meet real-time constraints, detectors typically adopt lightweight backbones and carefully designed computational modules, which inevitably reduce their ability to capture high-level semantics and lead to a semantic bottleneck.
Given the significant architectural and learning objective disparities between VFMs and resource-constrained detectors, achieving stable and taskaligned semantic transfer is challenging.
Such indirect supervision may be insufficient to fully optimize F5

background.summary: Builds on RT-DETR's hybrid encoder (AIFI + CCFF) and on RT-DETRv2/RT-DETRv3/D-FINE/DEIM training improvements, arguing that as architectural efficiency saturates, training supervision and semantic representation become the primary levers; VFMs such as DINOv3 supply high-capacity semantics.

relatedWork.name: RT-DETR
relatedWork.relation: base architecture the method is applied to; first real-time DETR
relatedWork.quote: RT-DETR [38] marked a milestone as the first real-time DETR, introducing the DETR family to the real-time community by outperforming YOLO models in both speed and accuracy.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: set-prediction paradigm that removed anchor design and NMS
relatedWork.quote: the DETR series has reshaped the detection paradigm through its unified modeling of object queries and set-based prediction.

relatedWork.name: DINOv3
relatedWork.relation: frozen semantic teacher used by the Deep Semantic Injector
relatedWork.quote: DINOv3 [31] demonstrates the scalability and efficacy of large-scale self-supervised learning, achieving rich and robust representations without human annotations.

relatedWork.name: D-FINE / DEIM
relatedWork.relation: prior training-side improvements that the paper builds on
relatedWork.quote: D-FINE [26] employed self-distillation to refine semantic representation, and DEIM [15] introduced dense matching for more precise feature alignment.

evidence.quote: Collectively, these developments illustrate a clear trend: as architectural efficiency saturates, training supervision and semantic representation become the primary levers for further progress.
Our work builds on this insight by strengthening the core representation via deep semantic transfer, achieving higher accuracy at no additional deployment or inference cost.

solution.summary: A training-only distillation framework aligning the detector's AIFI output feature F5 with frozen DINOv3 teacher features via a Deep Semantic Injector (linear projector + cosine loss), plus Gradient-guided Adaptive Modulation that tunes the loss weight from gradient-norm ratios.
solution.approach: Inject VFM semantics into the AIFI output feature F5 during training only, with an adaptively weighted alignment loss so the detector architecture and inference cost stay unchanged.
components: Deep Semantic Injector (DSI), a training-only module supervising F5
linear Feature Projector aligning resolution and channels with the teacher
cosine similarity alignment loss between projected detector and teacher features
Gradient-guided Adaptive Modulation (GAM) adjusting the loss weight by AIFI gradient-norm ratio
unchanged architecture and inference pipeline at deployment

evidence.quote: distillation framework that leverages the powerful representational capacity of VFMs to enhance lightweight object detectors.
we introduce a Deep Semantic Injector (DSI) module that facilitates the integration of high-level representations from VFMs into the deep layers of the detector.
we devise a Gradient-guided Adaptive Modulation (GAM) strategy, which dynamically adjusts the intensity of semantic transfer based on gradient norm ratios.
The proposed framework operates only during the training phase

experiments.summary: Evaluates on COCO 2017 with COCO AP metrics and T4 TensorRT FP16 latency, comparing RT-DETRv4 S/M/L/X against recent YOLO and DETR-based detectors, with ablations over injection position, projector, alignment loss and GAM versus static weights.

evidence.quote: model family, RT-DETRv4, achieves state-of-the-art results on COCO, attaining AP scores of 49.7/53.5/55.4/57.0 at corresponding speeds of 273/169/124/78 FPS.
Specifically, our RT-DETRv4-L achieves 55.4 AP on COCO at 124 FPS, outperforming YOLOv13-L (53.4 AP) and DEIM-L (54.7 AP) under comparable or even lower computational budgets.
Our method brings consistent and significant gains with zero additional inference cost.

limitations.summary: No dedicated limitations section; evident constraints are the COCO/RT-DETR-focused evaluation, marginal gains from DSI alone, the need for a frozen VFM teacher at training time, and DEIMv2-X still reporting higher AP than RT-DETRv4-X.
items: Empirical scope is COCO 2017 with RT-DETR-based detectors (plus a few DETR baselines for ablation)
DSI without GAM gives only slight improvements (about +0.1 to +0.2 AP)
Training requires a pre-trained frozen DINOv3-ViT-B teacher, adding training-time cost
DEIMv2-X still surpasses RT-DETRv4-X in AP, though at higher latency

evidence.quote: we focus on applying our framework to DETRbased real-time object detectors, i.e., RT-DETR models [38].
applying DSI can bring a slight performance improvement
Although DEIMv2-X achieves stronger performance, its latency is also higher than that of RT-DETRv4-X.

futureDirections.quote: This flexibility also opens up promising directions for multi-VFM semantic integration

futureDirections.quote: It can flexibly incorporate different foundation models, such as DINOv3 [31], MAE [13], or CLIP [27], and even benefit from arbitrarily large models for distilling semantics into real-time detectors.

applications.quote: such as autonomous driving [5], embodied intelligence [21]

applications.quote: This deployment-friendly property is crucial for industrial applications, where real-time detectors are tightly integrated into existing systems and hardware-constrained environments.
applications.detail: Deployment-friendly detector intended for tightly integrated, hardware-constrained industrial systems.

applications.quote: Since neither the detector structure nor the optimization pipeline is modified by the incorporation of VFMs, the additional training cost remains minimal.
applications.detail: Minimal training/structure overhead so the method extends to edge and large-scale deployment.

deploymentClaims: Our method introduces zero modification to detector architectures and does not alter the inference pipeline, ensuring that no additional computational cost or latency is incurred.
Without increasing deployment and inference overhead, our approach painlessly delivers striking and consistent performance gains across diverse DETR-based models
inference latency (in milliseconds) is measured on a single NVIDIA T4 GPU under TensorRT FP16 precision
